To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Bayesian CRLB, which is the most popular bound for parameter estimation, is not always tight; (ii) the Bayesian Cram er Rao lower bound (CRB) for the parameter estimation is a special case of the Bayesian CRB for the nonlinear filtering; (iii) the Bayesian CRB is always tighter than the Bayesian CRLBs, which are special cases of the Bayesian CRBs, for both the parameter estimation and the nonlinear filtering; and (iv) the

the Bayesian Cramer-Rao bound, Bayesian Bhattacharyyah bound, and Bobrovsky-Zakai bound are the same for both the Bayesian and frequentist approaches, and the Weiss-Weinstein bound is the same for the Bayesian approach, and different from that for the frequentist approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating a set of parameters in the presence of random noise.
the derivation and evaluation of Bayesian bounds on the estimation of unknown parameters in a dynamic system, and on the estimation of the unknown parameters in the dynamic system itself.
the development and analysis of bounds for parameter estimation, nonlinear filtering, and nonlinear tracking in the Bayesian context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bayesian bounds are not only the best known bounds, but they are also the most general and flexible bounds available.
the Bayesian approach is the most powerful approach to estimation theory.
, in general, the Bayesian bounds for parameter and state estimation are more informative than the corresponding non Bayesian bounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach to parameter estimation and nonlinear tracking, which is based on the Bayesian approach.

we are developing a theory for the design of optimal Bayesian estimators for a variety of signal estimation problems, including the estimation of parameters, signals, and states in the presence of noise.
we have developed a set of Bayesian bounds for the estimation of the parameters of the model and the state of the system in a nonlinear filtering/tracking problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bayesian bound for parameter estimation and filtering can be derived from the same basic principles, and the Bayesian bounds for parameter and signal estimation can be derived from each other.
the Bayesian Cramer Rao bound is a useful tool in parameter estimation, even when the underlying model is not linear and Gaussian.
the Bayesian Cramér-Rao bound (CRB), which is the standard benchmark for parameter estimation, is not the tightest bound for all cases of interest.
